title: Site authority and laboratory access
audience: Cleaners who may be asked to enter laboratories, and their supervisors.
learningOutcomes: Confirm that a named laboratory contact has released the documented room, zone and time window.
Recognise that a cleaning ticket does not override a restricted-entry sign.
Deny entry while an experiment is active, and defer the task with a record.

instruction.heading: A laboratory is not an ordinary room
instruction.body: A laboratory holds people, equipment, chemicals, samples and experiments that may be in progress. Some rooms are shared between groups, some hold material that must not be disturbed, and some have controls on who may enter and when. A cleaner who treats a laboratory as an office with more glassware will eventually disturb something that cannot be restored: a running incubator, a cold chain, a sealed sample, a bench that has been left in a particular state for a reason. This lesson concerns the first step, which is not cleaning at all. It is establishing whether you may enter, which parts you may enter, and when. Everything in later lessons depends on getting this step right. Laboratory decontamination, the handling of biological waste and biosafety-level work are specialist programmes. They are not general housekeeping, and nothing in this lesson teaches them.

instruction.heading: Who gives the release
instruction.body: A cleaning booking is a request. It shows that someone asked for a room to be cleaned on a date. It does not show who controls the room, whether it is occupied, or whether an experiment is in progress. The person who can release the room is normally the named laboratory contact, such as the laboratory manager, the chief investigator or the facilities contact the site has named, and the release should be in writing. The release should state the room, the zone within the room, the time window, the tasks allowed and the tasks excluded, and any conditions such as escort or protective equipment. If the site uses a separate facilities or safety officer, that officer may also need to confirm the release. Where the release is verbal, record who gave it and when, and ask for written confirmation before you enter. If the contact is not available, the room is not released.

instruction.heading: Reading the signs and the status
instruction.body: Before you enter, read the door. Look for restricted-entry signs, biological or chemical hazard signs, notices that name a responsible person, and any status indicator the site uses, such as a light, a board or a sign that shows an experiment is running. Where the sign is unclear, or the indicator is not set, treat the room as not released. A cleaning ticket never overrides a restricted-entry sign, and it does not cancel a notice placed by the person who controls the room. If a sign has been removed or looks old, do not assume it no longer applies. Ask the named contact, and record the answer. Do not enter to check whether an experiment is running, because your entry may be the disturbance the sign was placed to prevent.

instruction.heading: When an experiment is active
instruction.body: An active experiment means the room is in use, even if nobody is standing at a bench. Equipment may be running, samples may be incubating, and a bench may be set up for a process that must not be interrupted. The correct response is to deny entry for the period the experiment is active, to tell the named contact that the task has been deferred, and to record the deferral with the time, the reason, the person told and the new window requested. Do not clean around the experiment, do not move equipment, and do not wipe a surface you think is 'safe'. If the laboratory contact says that the experiment will run for a long time, agree a new window in writing, and keep the original booking on hold rather than cancelling it without a record.

instruction.heading: Your scope and the handover
instruction.body: Once you have a written release, the release defines your scope. A release for general floor cleaning in a corridor does not cover benches, fume enclosures, freezers or cabinets. A release for a shared office inside the laboratory does not cover the bench area. Where the scope is unclear, ask before you start. At the end of the visit, record what you did, which zones you did not enter, and what you left as found. Do not write that the laboratory is clean, decontaminated or safe. Those words belong to the laboratory's own procedures and to the competent people who make such statements. Your handover states the release, the scope and the areas you did not enter.

procedure: Check the booking and identify the room, the zone and the time window requested.
Ask the named laboratory contact to confirm the release in writing, stating the room, zone, time window, allowed tasks and excluded tasks.
Read the door and the room for restricted-entry signs, hazard signs and any experiment status indicator before you enter.
If the release is not given, or any sign or status indicator is unclear, do not enter. Record the reason.
If an experiment is active, deny entry for that period, tell the named contact, and record the deferral with the time, reason, person told and the new window.
Enter only the zones in the written release, and do not move, open or wipe equipment, samples or benches outside it.
At the end of the visit, record the zones cleaned, the zones not entered, the state left and the person who signed the handover.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaning ticket for 'Lab 3, Tuesday 7am' reaches your phone. When you arrive, the door has a restricted-entry sign with a named responsible person and a note that reads 'experiment in progress, do not enter'.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you enter, and what do you record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not enter. The cleaning ticket does not override the restricted-entry sign, and the note says an experiment is in progress. Contact the named responsible person or the laboratory contact, and tell them the task is deferred. Record the ticket, the sign, the time of arrival, the person contacted and the new window they give you in writing. Do not peek through the door to check the experiment, and do not clean the corridor section of the room if the release does not cover it.

workedExamples.situation: A laboratory manager tells you on the phone that the room is free and you may clean it. There is no written release, and the sign on the door is an older notice that refers to a completed project.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the verbal release enough, and what do you do?
workedExamples.reasoning: The verbal release is not enough on its own. Ask the laboratory manager to confirm the release in writing, stating the room, zone, time window, allowed and excluded tasks. Ask whether the older notice still applies or has been removed. Record the call, the names, the time, and the written confirmation when it arrives. Do not enter until the confirmation is in writing and the sign question is answered. If the answer is not clear, hold the task.

equipmentAndPpe: Written release form, or the site's equivalent, stating room, zone, time window, allowed and excluded tasks.
Access log and the site's sign-in and sign-out record.
Deferral record for any task that is held or deferred.

PPE as set by the site for the laboratory, including any eye protection, gloves or footwear the laboratory contact specifies. Do not select chemical or biological PPE for a laboratory you have not been released to enter.
Contact details for the named laboratory contact and the site's safety officer.

commonErrors.error: Treating a cleaning booking as permission to enter a laboratory.
commonErrors.prevention: A booking is a request. Obtain a written release from the named contact before you enter.

commonErrors.error: Entering because the sign looks old or the room seems empty.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat the room as not released until the sign question is answered in writing by the person who controls the room.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning around an active experiment, or moving equipment to clean under it.
commonErrors.prevention: Deny entry while the experiment is active, defer the task, and record the deferral.

commonErrors.error: Writing that the laboratory is clean, decontaminated or safe at the end of the visit.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the zones cleaned, the zones not entered and the state left. Leave any safety or decontamination statement to the competent person.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Under the model WHS framework, the business or undertaking that controls a workplace has a primary duty to manage risks to health and safety so far as is reasonably practicable. Where more than one party shares a duty for the same risk, each must consult and coordinate with the others. Safe Work Australia's current model code on biological hazards restates this, and it says that the duty holder must provide information, training, instruction or supervision needed to protect others. Its appendices on cleaning, hygiene and PPE were not read for this lesson.
Laboratory decontamination, the handling of biological waste and biosafety-level work are specialist programmes and not general cleaning.

Chemicals in a laboratory must be identified before any contact. The manufacturer or importer prepares the safety data sheet, which must be reviewed at least every five years and must cover handling and disposal.
This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate, biosafety approval or specialist authority, and completing it does not make a cleaner competent to enter or work in a restricted laboratory.

qualityStandard: Every entry in the case study is preceded by a written release that names the room, zone, time window, allowed tasks and excluded tasks.
The case study with an active experiment is deferred, with the deferral recorded, and no entry is made.
The closing handover lists the zones cleaned, the zones not entered and the state left, and contains no safety or decontamination statement.
documentationEvidence: Written release from the named laboratory contact, with room, zone, time window, allowed and excluded tasks.
Access log with sign-in and sign-out times and the name of each person who entered.
Deferral record with time, reason, person told and the new window requested.
Closing handover with zones cleaned, zones not entered and the state left.
summary: A cleaning booking is a request. Only a written release from the named contact allows entry.
A restricted-entry sign or an active experiment stops the task, whatever the booking says.
Defer the task with a record, and agree a new window in writing.
Record the zones entered and not entered, and leave safety and decontamination statements to competent people.

knowledgeChecks.question: A cleaning ticket is booked for a laboratory. Does that let you enter?
options: Yes, the booking is the permission to enter the room and the zone for the clean
No, you need a written release from the named laboratory contact for the room, zone and time
Yes, if the room door is unlocked and nobody has objected to the entry at all

knowledgeChecks.question: An experiment is active in the room. What is the correct action?
options: Clean the room quietly around the experiment, keeping well back from it
Deny entry for that period, tell the named contact, and record the deferral
Move the equipment to one side so that the floor can be cleaned

knowledgeChecks.question: What may the handover say about a cleaned laboratory?
options: That the laboratory is clean, decontaminated and safe for the next user and the staff who work there
The zones cleaned, the zones not entered and the state left, with no safety or decontamination statement
That the laboratory is ready for use, as the cleaner has finished the job and the room is clear
